title: Transitioning to Involutional Neural Network For Resource Efficient Federated Plant Disease Classification
description: This study endeavors to develop an efficient and privacy-preserving methodology for classifying plant diseases utilizing Involutional Neural Networks (InvNets) within a federated learning framework. The methodology utilizes two comprehensive datasets, NewPlantDisease and PlantVillage, which are distributed across multiple clients to enable decentralized training and safeguard data privacy. Image preprocessing encompasses resizing to 128×128 pixels, converting to RGB format, and applying augmentation techniques such as cropping to enrich dataset diversity. InvNets, employing location-specific and channel-agnostic kernels, are implemented and juxtaposed with conventional convolutional models, including VGG16, ResNet-50, and MobileNet V2. The models are trained locally on client devices, and their updates are consolidated at a central server, ensuring the non-disclosure of raw data and preserving privacy. Performance evaluation incorporates metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and confusion matrices. This comprehensive approach aims to showcase the superior efficiency and effectiveness of InvNets in terms of classification accuracy and resource utilization, thereby enhancing agricultural sustainability and food security while upholding robust data privacy.
